text:
Two days before a teenager killed a young girl while in the grips of psychosis, her father dismissed her homicidal thoughts, delusions and visions as “crap”, an inquest has been told.
On 6 July 2020, the 14-year-old wrote in her diary: “I’m getting sick and tired of being told I’m a liar when I say I see cat eyes in a dark room and feel like I’m going to kill someone.”
Just 48 hours later, the teenager killed 10-year-old Bridgette “Biddy” Porter at a property in rural NSW.
Biddy, remembered as a clever, creative and kind child, died of multiple injuries while staying at the farm in the school holidays on 8 July 2020.
The details of her death are subject to a non-publication order.
During closing submissions at an inquest on Thursday, the barrister representing Biddy’s parents argued it was unreasonable for the teenager’s parents not to seek urgent help.
“It is open to this court to make findings there were a constellation of symptoms they were aware of,” Tahn O’Rourke told the NSW coroner’s court in Lidcombe on Thursday.
“They were aware they were linked … and that there was a potentially serious mental illness emerging.”
The teenager killed six chickens on the family farm in mid-2019 and subsequently told relatives about hearing voices, experiencing visions and having a sense of not feeling real, the inquest was told.
In the weeks before attacking Biddy, the teenager told her mother she thought about killing people “all the time”, including her parents.
The mother said she did not seek mental health support for the girl because it did not occur to her.
“I never believed in mental health. I didn’t understand mental health, so it didn’t come up to me as something I needed to do,” she told the inquest in June.
The father’s police statement said he told the teenager her visions and violent thoughts were “crap and she was just looking for attention”, O’Rourke said.
The mother sought advice from a naturopath in mid-2020, who told her to go to a GP.
The GP referred the family to a psychiatrist soon before the killing, but didn’t organise urgent care because the mother did not reveal the teenager’s violence or homicidal thoughts, the inquest was told.
That was an “opportunity lost” in preventing harm, O’Rourke said.
Biddy’s killer, who cannot be identified, was charged with murder, but a NSW supreme court judge ruled she was not criminally responsible due to mental illness in 2021.
The teenager, who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia and was in acute psychosis at the time of the killing, remains in a forensic facility.
Counsel assisting Dr Peggy Dwyer SC said the actions of the parents should be seen in the context of evidence that early symptoms of schizophrenia can be “vague” and hard to separate from typical teenage behaviour.
Forensic psychiatrist Olav Nielssen gave evidence the girl’s early development of schizophrenia was “extremely rare” and he had never seen a presentation like hers before.
Dwyer said there was a gap in the parents’ understanding.
“[They] were not aware [she] was suffering a serious mental health condition … even if looking back now, it seems so obvious,” Dwyer said.
State coroner Teresa O’Sullivan will hand down findings and recommendations at a later date.

digest_he:
ועדת חקירה באוסטרליה דנה בנסיבות מותה של הילדה ברדג'ט פורטר, שנרצחה בשנת 2020 על ידי נערה בת 14 שסבלה מאפיזודה פסיכוטית. לפי העדויות, יומיים לפני הרצח כתבה הנערה ביומנה כי היא חשה תסכול מכך שמתייחסים אליה כאל שקרנית כאשר היא מדווחת על הזיות ותחושות קשות.

נציגי משפחת הקורבן טענו בוועדה כי ההורים התרשלנו בכך שלא ביקשו עזרה נפשית דחופה למרות שהיו מודעים לשינויים בהתנהגותה ולתסמינים נפשיים מדאיגים. בשנת 2021 קבע בית המשפט כי הנערה אינה אחראית פלילית למעשיה בשל מחלת נפש, והיא מאושפזת כיום במתקן רפואי-משפטי.
